title: New start-era pin contradicts the PP_DEBUG define and ships the CI debug-test leg red
evidence: app/pullback_test.odin:560: `testing.expectf(t, app_start_era() == u8(1), "the shipped start era must be Foundations (1), got %d", app_start_era())` | app/main.odin:53: `APP_ERA :: u8(3)`; app/main.odin:57-62: `app_start_era :: proc() -> u8 {` / `when #config(PP_DEBUG, false) {` / `return APP_ERA` / `} else {` / `return APP_START_ERA` | .github/workflows/ci.yml:135: `odin test app -define:PP_DEBUG=true -out:bin/app-debug-test`
detail: Under the CI-pinned -define:PP_DEBUG=true leg, app_start_era() returns APP_ERA (3), not 1, so the new test fails that existing gate; the fixture comment even plans for the define build ('Rows run to APP_ERA so PP_DEBUG override builds work too').
recommended_fix: Guard the expectation with `when #config(PP_DEBUG, false)` (expect APP_ERA in the debug branch), or drop the literal-1 pin and keep the define-agnostic `app.state.era == app_start_era()` assertion.

title: check_reject_balance still passes on wrong-file rejections — the vacuity-enabling early-return survives the B1 fix
evidence: core/catalog_test.odin:1209-1212: `if cerr.file != "balance.json" {` / `testing.expectf(t, cerr.file != "", "expected a balance.json rejection (rule %q), got %q %q", want_rule, cerr.file, cerr.rule)` / `return` / `}` — vs the strict sibling, core/catalog_test.odin:434: `testing.expectf(t, cerr.file == "balance.json", "rejection file: got %q want balance.json", cerr.file)`
detail: A wrong-file rejection still returns success — exactly how the vacuous table passed when the crises source was missing. Any future source-order change silently re-creates B1; the strict sibling hard-asserts the file.
recommended_fix: Make check_reject_balance hard-assert cerr.file == "balance.json" like check_reject_bal, or delete the lenient helper and route all rows through the strict one.

title: Rebuilt BAL_* constants restate BAL_VALID wholesale instead of deriving via replace1 like sibling rows
evidence: core/catalog_test.odin:111-115: `// BAL_NO_PRESETS / BAL_EMPTY_PRESETS / BAL_BAD_PRESET_ID - the r3 B1 rebuild:` / `BAL_NO_PRESETS :: \`{"logic_hz": 20, ...` — three ~44-line literals duplicating BAL_VALID's body (warnings/health/box/advance/ladder/placement/map blocks identical); the established sibling style, e.g. core/catalog_test.odin:828ff: `{"ladder missing", replace1(BAL_VALID, `[ ... ],`, ``, 1), "must be an array of 3 rows (1/2/3 in-play lanes)"}`
detail: ~130 duplicated JSON lines must be hand-synced whenever BAL_VALID gains a required block; every other negative row derives its variant with a replace1 one-liner on BAL_VALID.
recommended_fix: Derive the three variants with replace1 on BAL_VALID (drop the presets block / empty it / blank the preset id), matching the table's established convention.

title: crises_resolved is write-only — incremented, never read, printed, or gated on
evidence: harness/econ.odin:44: `crises_resolved: i32, // internal: Crisis_Resolved events seen` ; harness/econ.odin:96: `if e.tag == pp.EVENT_TAG_CRISIS_RESOLVED do stats.crises_resolved += 1` — repo-wide grep finds no other reference; econ_print_row's format string omits it and no econ_check verdict reads it
detail: Dead instrumentation: the counter suggests crisis-resolution evidence the sim never reports or asserts, unlike its sibling dots_during_crisis which the Q7 verdict consumes.
recommended_fix: Either print it in econ_print_row as crisis-stall resolution evidence (or gate a verdict on it), or drop the field.
